title: Lapland: 5.2 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €211,500 a year
markdown:
# Lapland: 5.2 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €211,500 a year

> Closes 5.2 of 12.1 missing patients a year (43%) · €211,500 of €1M · €788,500 left: nothing more pays off on today's evidence

## The gap

Of 100 lung cancer patients in Lapland, 18 get treatment that aims to cure. In Finland it is 27. That is about 12 patients a year. [^care_curative] Versus the best quarter of counties, 16.8 a year are missing (range 12.6–20.8) [^model]. Against Finland: 7.4 fewer operated, 4.7 fewer given radiotherapy that aims to cure [^model]. Diagnosis-to-treatment waits in the OYS collaborative area are no longer: 31.2 days, Finland 36.9 [^care_time_to_treatment]. Fewer are treated to cure [^care_curative]. Residents' age predicts 24.6%; Lapland reaches 18.5% [^model]. Part of the gap may be treatment given but not recorded [^care_no_record].

## The target

Raise the share of lung cancer patients treated to cure from 18.5% to 22.2% by 2028: 5.2 more patients a year (range 0.0–7.7), for €211,500 a year, about €40,363 per extra patient. [^care_curative][^model] That closes 43% of the measured shortfall against Finland as a whole (12.1 patients a year). [^model]

## Funded actions

| # | Action and owner | Cost a year | More patients treated to cure a year (range) | First step this week | Measure: today → target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **Step zero: fix the records (no direct effect)** | | | | |
| 0 | **Audit of treatment records ("no treatment on record")**[^ev_recording_audit_1]. Chief physician of oncology and the head of clinical coding | €8,000 | 0.0 | Pull 50 patients diagnosed in 2023 with no treatment on record and check their charts this month. | Share of patients with no treatment on record: 33.8% → 27.5% by 2027 |
| | **The county can start on Monday** | | | | |
| 1 | **Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated**[^ev_sbrt_pathway_1]. Chief physician of oncology; chief of radiotherapy at the university hospital | €30,400 | 1.1 (0.0–2.3) | Write the referral rule: every stage I patient not accepted for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy the same week. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 18.5% → 19.3% by 2028 |
| 2 | **Travel and accommodation support for patients far from the university hospital**[^ev_travel_accommodation_support_1]. Chief physician of oncology and hospital social work; university hospital patient hotel | €43,600 | 0.7 (0.0–0.7) | Name one contact person who books the patient hotel and transport for every patient sent to the university hospital for curative treatment. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 18.5% → 19.0% by 2028 |
| 3 | **Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment**[^ev_prehab_fitness_assessment_1]. Chief physician of pulmonology; leads of rehabilitation and geriatrics | €37,500 | 0.3 (0.0–0.3) | Decide that no stage I-III patient is recorded as "not fit" without an exercise test, and book the physiotherapy group. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 18.5% → 18.7% by 2028 |
| | **Needs the collaborative area (university hospital)** | | | | |
| 4 | **Thoracic surgeon reviews every decision not to operate**[^ev_surgeon_second_opinion_1]. Chief physician of pulmonology; chief of thoracic surgery at the university hospital | €41,000 | 1.7 (0.0–3.4) | Agree with the university hospital that a thoracic surgeon joins the weekly lung meeting, and send last quarter's stage I-II patients who were not operated for a second look. | Share of patients operated: 9.8% → 11.0% by 2028 |
| 5 | **Video MDT review of every stage I-III patient with the university hospital**[^ev_video_mdt_stage1_3_1]. Chief physician of pulmonology; lead of the university hospital lung MDT | €51,000 | 1.4 (0.0–1.6) | Ask the university hospital for a fixed weekly video slot and list every stage I-III patient diagnosed last month who was not discussed there. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 18.5% → 19.5% by 2028 |
| | **Total** | **€211,500** | **5.2 (0.0–7.7)** | | |

No trial has measured these effects; the low end of every range is zero. The ranges do not add up to the range of the total, because the measures share one ceiling. Costs are assumptions. [^model]

## Needs a national decision (outside this budget)

- **Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers**[^ev_ldct_screening_1]: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko (decision), Finnish Cancer Registry (steering), county (delivery). €548,645 a year; modelled to avoid 0.9 deaths a year (0.2–2.4). Not counted in this budget. Not a county decision. Ask the Ministry and Palko for the timetable after the 2026-2028 pilot and offer the county as a pilot site. [^model]

## What to measure from Monday

- Share of patients treated to cure: 18.5% (2019–2023, measured) → 22.2% by 2028. [^care_curative][^model]
- Share of patients with no treatment on record: 33.8% → 27.5% by 2027. [^care_no_record][^model]
- Share of patients operated: 9.8% → 11.0% by 2028. [^care_surgery][^model]
- The registry's public figures cover 2019–2023; count these each month from the county's own records. [^care_curative]

## What more money buys, and what it cannot

In the model, the remaining €788,500 buys nothing more toward this goal: the €211,500 plan already funds every measure that adds patients treated to cure, limited by the reachable part of the shortfall, not by money [^model]. More could come from low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers, which needs a national decision, or from ranking measures by deaths avoided instead [^model]. Lung cancer causes about 110 deaths a year in Lapland; this plan is modelled to avoid 0.8 of them [^deaths] [^model].

## Pilot ask

Six-month pilot: surgeon review + radiotherapy referral. The two actions model 2.8 extra patients/year and 20.5% treated to cure by 2028. Six months cannot show the share moving; it can show the pathway work. [^model]

## Limits

- Effect ranges are not probabilities: they run from every assumed effect at its lowest to every one at its highest; no trial has measured these effects [^model].
- The expected share is adjusted only for residents' age, not stage, fitness, other illness, histology, how the cancer was found or smoking; county figures cannot show cause [^model].
- 33.8% have no treatment on record (Finland 27.5%); some treatment may be given but unrecorded, so audit records before reading this as a gap in care [^care_no_record].
